learning_outcomes.text: Knows the intermediate grammatical structures of the English language and specific communicative functions of B1 B2 CEFR levels;
Understands expressions and connectors used to express condition, purpose, cause, consequence and preferences;
Has knowledge of general technical vocabulary, necessary in real-life and professional contexts;
Understands elements of Anglo-Saxon culture and civilization, relevant for academic and professional interactions;
Is familiar with written and oral communication conventions (formulating requests, opinions, proposals, etc.).
Uses correct grammatical and lexical structures in written and oral expression, in real and simulated situations;
Drafts messages, requests, instructions, and replies, respecting English language norms;
Applies communicative functions to request and offer information, to express opinions, agreement/disagreement, and proposals;
Actively participates in dialogues, discussions, and group activities in English;
Uses authentic materials (audio, video, written) to improve linguistic competences.
Assumes responsibility for their own linguistic training and uses additional resources for improvement;
Collaborates effectively with colleagues in seminar activities and contributes to the accomplishment of common tasks;
Respects polite interaction rules, in teams or individually, in multicultural contexts;
Shows initiative in using the English language in practical contexts, demonstrating openness and adaptability;
Self-evaluates and monitors personal progress in the development of linguistic competences.

syllabus_topics: Expressing purpose; specific markers and connectors; using information in situational contexts with technical specificity
Expressing cause; specific markers and connectors; using information in situational contexts with technical specificity
Expressing consequence; specific markers and connectors; using information in situational contexts with technical specificity
Synoptic revision of the interrogative form; formulating requests, expressing preference, requesting information and/or opinions in specific and diverse real contexts

Specificities of imperative use; formulating requests, assigning tasks to a group; explaining rules, formulating instructions, expressing politeness; expressing prohibition; instructions and precautions

assessment_methods.method: Active participation in seminar activities and evaluation test

assessment_rules: The final evaluation result for a discipline is obtained by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity within the discipline. Integer grades from 1 to 10 will be awarded, with a grade of 5 certifying the achievement of the minimum learning outcomes for a discipline and the granting of the associated study credits. A minimum grade of 5 is required for both the exam component and the seminar component.
